content_html:
NexusMem

Your coding agent can read git log. It cannot read the four things you tried last Tuesday that didn't work.

NexusMem records what actually happened on your machine (shell commands and their exit codes, git history down to the patch of each changed file, project docs, optionally your assistant transcripts) into a local SQLite database, and serves back a ranked, token-budgeted slice of it on demand. Everything stays on disk. No account, no cloud, no telemetry.

The shell history is the part worth caring about. Git tells an agent what shipped. Shell history tells it what was attempted, in what order, and which commands exited non-zero. That information exists nowhere else, and it disappears when your terminal scrollback rolls over.

Try it

From inside any git repository:

npx nexusmem init
npx nexusmem sync

Then ask it something. Real output from this repository, top 2 of 5 hits:

$ nexusmem query "windows spawn failure"

Relevant history for: windows spawn failure

- 2026-08-09 fix: distinguish a failed git spawn from "not a git repository"
  readRepoInfo collapsed three unrelated failures into one error: git running and reporting
  the path is not a work tree, git not being installed, and the process failing to spawn at
  all. Dogfooding hit the third case in two separate sessions...
- 2026-08-09 README.md — Before a tagged release
  - [ ] Retry on transient process-spawn failures on Windows

A commit and a docs section, ranked against each other, inside whatever token budget you gave it. Nothing was summarized by a model on the way out; the ranker just decided what not to send. (One optional source, session summaries, does run a local model — but at ingest time, never on the way out. What you query is always stored text.)

For a sense of what actually accumulates, here is nexusmem status on this repo after two days:

527 node(s)  2026-08-08 .. 2026-08-09
       321  shell_command
       130  conversation_turn
        60  doc_section
        16  git_commit

Sixteen commits. Three hundred and twenty-one shell commands. The commits were already retrievable by any agent with a terminal. The rest was not.

That conversation_turn row only appears because this corpus was synced with --conversation. Assistant transcripts are the one source that is off by default and stays off until you opt in, since they are the likeliest place for a pasted credential to be sitting. A default install indexes git commits, their diffs, shell and docs.

Requirements: Node 22 or newer, and git. Node 20 will not work, because better-sqlite3 ships no prebuilt binary for it and Node 20 went end-of-life in April 2026. Ollama is optional and only affects semantic search (see below).

Optional: exact shell capture

Scraped history files (PSReadLine, .bash_history, .zsh_history) give you command text and not much else. The hook gives you working directory, exit code and a real timestamp:

nexusmem hook install

It wraps your existing PowerShell prompt rather than replacing it, is idempotent, and nexusmem hook remove undoes it cleanly.

Exit codes are what make this worth installing. A failed command is a stronger signal than a successful one, and without the hook there is no way to tell them apart.

How retrieval works

Every source normalizes to the same MemoryNode shape, so a commit, a shell command and a docs section compete on equal terms. Retrieval runs BM25 over FTS5 and, if an embedding model is reachable, a vector search over sqlite-vec, then fuses the two with Reciprocal Rank Fusion.

RRF fuses on rank position only, never on raw scores. That is the entire reason it is safe here: a BM25 cost and a vector distance live on unrelated, unbounded scales, and position is the only thing they agree on. No hand-tuned normalization constant sits between them.

Ranking then multiplies three factors:

score = relevance × signal^0.215 × recency^0.288

relevance comes from the query. signal (a fix: commit outranks a chore:; a command that exited non-zero outranks one that succeeded) and recency are priors that hold before any query exists. Each factor is floored into [floor, 1] rather than [0, 1], so one weak dimension cannot zero out a strong match.

Those exponents are derived, not tuned. Priors kept overturning the query: on one real query a fix: commit took rank 1 from a better-matching docs section on a 44% signal edge against a 15% relevance deficit. So the priors get a shared budget — across their whole range they may overturn at most a 2× relevance gap — split evenly between them, and each is raised to the power that makes its own span worth exactly its share (span^exponent = √2). Priors still order equally-relevant hits exactly as before, since the transform is monotonic. They just cannot outvote the question anymore.

The budget is shared rather than per-prior for a reason found by dogfooding, not by reading the arithmetic: the score multiplies the priors, so capping each at 2× separately left the pair free to overturn 4×. That describes every commit made during an active working day — fresh and high-signal at once — so the failure landed on precisely the days with the most worth remembering. A query about the PowerShell hook returned two unrelated same-day fix: commits at ranks 3 and 4 while the section that answered it sat at rank 6. Adding a third prior now re-divides the same budget instead of enlarging it.

Without Ollama, vector search is skipped and you get BM25 only. That path is fully supported, not a degraded error state; sync and query both succeed and simply do less.

Session summaries (optional, local model)

With sources.session.enabled, each finished session becomes one distilled node next to the raw exchanges — what was decided and why, rather than forty individual turns. It runs a local Ollama chat model (qwen2.5:3b by default); nothing is downloaded automatically and nothing leaves the machine.

nexusmem scan-session --dry-run

That prints the exact prompt a session would produce, after redaction and budget trimming, without calling the model.

Three things bound the cost. A session is only summarized once it has been quiet for settleMinutes (default 30), so a session in progress is not re-summarized on every sync. The prompt is hashed, and an unchanged hash skips the model entirely — on this repo a steady-state sync of 14 summarized sessions takes 0.25s and makes no model calls. And maxSessions (default 10) caps how many reach the model per run; the rest are reported as queued and picked up next sync.

What it is actually like, measured on 14 real sessions with qwen2.5:3b. The summaries themselves are good: decisions with their reasons, in the shape the prompt asks for. Titles are less reliable — the model returned a usable one about a third of the time, and otherwise produced a conversational preamble, a stray bullet, or a bare "Summary of the Session". Those are rejected and the title falls back to the first line of the question that opened the session, which is always specific even when it is not elegant. Compliance was worst on long sessions and on transcripts not in English. A larger model (qwen2.5:7b) is the lever if the titles matter to you; set sources.session.model.

Use it from an agent

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "nexusmem": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "nexusmem", "mcp"]
    }
  }
}

Three tools over stdio: search_memory returns the packed context block, sync_project ingests, and get_status reports what is currently remembered. Each takes an explicit projectRoot, because an MCP tool call carries no shell working directory. sync_project runs init for you if the repository has not been set up.

What it costs you

Two numbers get conflated in tools like this, so they are kept apart here.

Packer efficiency is how much the ranker trims from its own candidate set. On this repository's corpus it runs 81–84%. It is useful for tuning the ranker and useless as a claim about your bill, because the baseline is hypothetical: without NexusMem those candidates were never going into your context window in the first place.

End-to-end saving compares the packed context NexusMem actually sends against reading, in full, the same files its own ranking identified as relevant to the query. Measured with scripts/benchmark.ts (npm run bench), which anyone who clones this repo and points it at a synced corpus can re-run from scratch:

Corpus Commits Query set vs. full file content vs. git log -p on those files
This repo 62 16 real prompts, verbatim from this project's own history 95% (median 94%) 98% (median 97%)
vitejs/vite 9,567 16, mechanically sampled — see below 99% (median 98%) ~100% (median ~100%) — see caveat

Both clear the original >70% target ("cut API token spend versus sending full context"), and the vite run is the first measurement at the scale that target was always described as applying to.

Read the methodology before quoting either number, because it is a narrower claim than it looks:

  • The file set each query is graded against comes from NexusMem's own ranking — whichever files the packed nodes for that query touch, not an outside judge's idea of the right answer. This isolates what the pack step (rank → budget → excerpt) saves once retrieval has already picked a candidate set; it does not independently verify that the candidate set was the right one to pick.
  • The vite query set is not hand-picked: an even sample, across the full commit history, of well-explained fix/feat/perf/refactor commits turned into "why does vite <description>" from the commit's own conventional-commit text, plus rationale-bearing doc section headings. This repo's own query set instead reuses real historical prompts verbatim from conversation_turn nodes — several are broad task instructions rather than narrow questions, which pulls a wider file set into scope and is part of why its number, while still high, sits below vite's. Both derivations are mechanical and disclosed in scripts/benchmark.ts, neither is cherry-picked per-query.
  • git log -p on a file touched by thousands of commits is enormous — one vite query's baseline hit 7.5M tokens because a file in its resolved set has that much history. That is itself a finding, not noise: at this scale, "just read the file's history instead" stops being a viable alternative at all, which is a big part of why that column rounds to ~100%.
  • This supersedes the previous ~40% figure, which was hand-tallied from two hand-picked queries against this repo alone, never instrumented, and used an unstated baseline. It was not wrong so much as underspecified — this number replaces it with a stated method and a script that reproduces it, rather than being a claim that the product got better.

One thing that is not a percentage: shell commands and conversation turns have no cheap grep equivalent. Without something recording them, they are gone, not merely more expensive to find.

Latency on a ~530-node corpus, warm, p50 over 10 runs:

Operation
BM25 retrieval (FTS5) ~1.1 ms
Vector KNN (sqlite-vec) ~3.2 ms
Fuse, rank, pack ~0.6 ms
Query embedding (local Ollama) ~55–77 ms
End-to-end hybrid ~56 ms

All the SQLite work totals about 5 ms. The embedding call is the only thing on this path worth optimizing, and it is somebody else's process.

Where it breaks

  • Shell history without the hook is unscoped. Scraped history has no directory context, so it is attributed to whichever repository you ran sync from. Bounded to a tail window, and an approximation rather than a guarantee.
  • Japanese and Chinese depend on the vector pass. FTS5's unicode61 tokenizer splits on whitespace, so languages without space boundaries get no useful BM25 recall.
  • Rebasing strands nodes. Rewritten history leaves nodes for unreachable commits. They describe real events so they are not wrong, but a targeted prune does not exist yet. sync --rebuild forces a clean re-scan.
  • Multi-line PowerShell input is read as separate commands. A function typed across several lines at the prompt is not reconstructed.
  • Scrape-fallback ids drift if the history file is trimmed from the front between syncs. Installing the hook fixes this.
  • Session-summary titles depend on the model following instructions, and a 3B model often does not. The fallback keeps them specific rather than generic, but see the section above for what to expect.
  • Changing the embedding model re-embeds everything. Vectors from two models are not comparable and nodes_vec records no per-row provenance, so sync drops the lot and rebuilds rather than ranking across a mixture. It says so when it happens. Nodes are untouched and BM25 keeps working throughout.
  • Diff indexing is bounded, and deliberately lossy. A first sync indexes the patches of the most recent 200 commits (later syncs only walk cursor..HEAD); merge commits contribute none, since their patch exists only in a combined format this parser does not read; and binaries, lockfiles and build output are skipped so a dependency bump cannot bury the corpus. All of it is still recorded as a git_commit node. A patch longer than limits.maxBodyChars is truncated, so the tail of a very large change is not indexed. The caps live under sources.diff in config.json.
  • Cross-project recall favours breadth. Each repository's hits are fused by rank, so a project whose best match is mediocre still contributes a rank-1 item, and rank 1 is worth the same in every list. Adding a repository that has little to say about your question still pushes a few of its results into the budget. Signal, recency and the budget are what hold that in check; there is no per-project quality weight.
  • The project registry is an index, not a source of truth. It can point at a database that has moved or been deleted; those are reported and skipped, never silently pruned, because an unmounted drive is not a deleted project.
  • Conversation chunking is unevaluated. Splitting long replies at heading boundaries measurably helped, but it has never been tested systematically.
  • A chunked node's sibling count in one result is capped, not tuned. conversation_turn and doc_section both split one reply or file into several nodes; at most 2 of them may appear together in a packed result. Found live: a query for "token" returned 9 of its top 12 hits as different pieces of one heavily-sectioned reply, crowding out the node that actually answered it. The cap of 2 is a judgement call, not a measured optimum, same as the ranking priors' budget above.
  • The size of the prior budget is a judgement call, not a measured optimum. Priors are now bounded jointly rather than one at a time, which closed a real 4× hole (see the ranking section), but the 2× budget itself has never been tuned against a labelled relevance set — there isn't one. It is a defensible constant, not a result. What is measured is the direction: on four real queries against this repo's own memory, switching to the joint cap moved the section that answered the question up in three of them (the rationale section for "why BM25 before vector search" went from rank 4 to rank 1) and displaced no query's correct top hit.

Commands

init, sync, query <text>, status, projects, mcp, and hook install|remove|status.

There are also five dry-run previews (scan-git, scan-diff, scan-shell, scan-docs, scan-conversation) that write nothing and print the nodes ingestion would create along with their signal scores. That is the intended way to tune scoring against a real repository before committing to a change. Add --json to pipe them somewhere.

Every command takes -C <path> to target another repository. On sync, --conversation opts the transcript source in for one run without persisting it, --no-embed skips the vector pass, and --rebuild drops the project's nodes and re-ingests from scratch.

Recall across projects

query --all-projects searches every repository you have run NexusMem in, not just the current one, and tags each result with the repository it came from:

$ nexusmem query --all-projects "why was the retry budget raised"
scope   2 project(s): NexusMem, uploader

- 2026-08-12 [uploader] fix: raise the retry budget after the S3 upload timeouts
- 2026-08-12 [uploader] retry.ts @ 8d0f98b — fix: raise the retry budget after the S3 upload timeouts
  @@ -1 +1 @@
  -export const RETRY_BUDGET = 3;
  +export const RETRY_BUDGET = 5;
- 2026-08-09 [NexusMem] fix(git): retry a transient failure to spawn git

Databases stay per-repository — there is no shared global store, and deleting one repo's .nexusmem/ still removes exactly that repo's memory. What makes the others findable is a plain index at ~/.nexusmem/projects.json, written by init and refreshed by every sync. nexusmem projects shows what is in it, and --prune forgets entries whose database is gone.

Ranking across repositories uses reciprocal rank fusion per project rather than raw BM25, because a BM25 cost is computed against its own corpus and means different things in a 50-node and a 50,000-node database. The trade is stated in Where it breaks.

The MCP search_memory tool takes the same switch as allProjects: true.

On disk

<repo>/.nexusmem/
  .gitignore     '*' — the workspace ignores itself, so init never edits a file it doesn't own
  config.json    validated on read; a corrupt config fails loudly rather than silently
  memory.db      SQLite in WAL mode

~/.nexusmem/
  projects.json      which repositories exist, for cross-project recall; a corrupt one reads as empty
  shell-history.jsonl  the hook's log, if you installed it

NEXUSMEM_HOME overrides the user-scoped directory.

Node ids are content-addressed from sha256(projectId + kind + naturalKey), so running sync twice cannot produce duplicates and ingestion stays correct even if a cursor is lost. Project identity comes from the normalized origin URL when there is one, falling back to the absolute path, so two clones of the same repo share one memory namespace.

Deleting .nexusmem/ loses nothing that sync cannot rebuild.

Status

Ingestion, hybrid retrieval, budgeted packing and the MCP server all work and are covered by 342 tests running on Linux and Windows across Node 22 and 24.

Development

npm install
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build

Tests are behavioral rather than snapshot-based, and several are regressions tied to specific observed failures. tests/git-errors.test.ts injects a fake spawn to exercise the Windows process-spawn faults, which cannot be provoked on demand.

On how this was built

This started as an experiment in whether a local context-memory engine for coding agents was viable, prototyped with Claude Code. The code was written through AI-assisted workflows; the architecture, the design decisions and the specifications were human-directed.

That is worth stating plainly because it should change how you read the code, not whether you trust it. Audits, corrections and PRs are genuinely welcome, and the commit history is deliberately detailed about why things are the way they are, including the times an earlier assumption turned out to be wrong.

Found live: a query for "token" returned 9 of its top 12 hits as different pieces of one heavily-sectioned reply, crowding out the node that actually answered it. The cap of 2 is a judgement call, not a measured optimum, same as the ranking priors' budget above. The size of the prior budget is a judgement call, not a measured optimum. Priors are now bounded jointly rather than one at a time, which closed a real 4× hole (see the ranking section), but the 2× budget itself has never been tuned against a labelled relevance set — there isn't one. It is a defensible constant, not a result. What is measured is the direction: on four real queries against this repo's own memory, switching to the joint cap moved the section that answered the question up in three of them (the rationale section for "why BM25 before vector search" went from rank 4 to rank 1) and displaced no query's correct top hit. Commands init, sync, query <text>, status, projects, mcp, and hook install|remove|status. There are also five dry-run previews (scan-git, scan-diff, scan-shell, scan-docs, scan-conversation) that write nothing and print the nodes ingestion would create along with their signal scores. That is the intended way to tune scoring against a real repository before committing to a change. Add --json to pipe them somewhere. Every command takes -C <path> to target another repository. On sync, --conversation opts the transcript source in for one run without persisting it, --no-embed skips the vector pass, and --rebuild drops the project's nodes and re-ingests from scratch. Recall across projects query --all-projects searches every repository you have run NexusMem in, not just the current one, and tags each result with the repository it came from: $ nexusmem query --all-projects "why was the retry budget raised" scope 2 project(s): NexusMem, uploader - 2026-08-12 [uploader] fix: raise the retry budget after the S3 upload timeouts - 2026-08-12 [uploader] retry.ts @ 8d0f98b — fix: raise the retry budget after the S3 upload timeouts @@ -1 +1 @@ -export const RETRY_BUDGET = 3; +export const RETRY_BUDGET = 5; - 2026-08-09 [NexusMem] fix(git): retry a transient failure to spawn git Databases stay per-repository — there is no shared global store, and deleting one repo's .nexusmem/ still removes exactly that repo's memory. What makes the others findable is a plain index at ~/.nexusmem/projects.json, written by init and refreshed by every sync. nexusmem projects shows what is in it, and --prune forgets entries whose database is gone. Ranking across repositories uses reciprocal rank fusion per project rather than raw BM25, because a BM25 cost is computed against its own corpus and means different things in a 50-node and a 50,000-node database. The trade is stated in Where it breaks. The MCP search_memory tool takes the same switch as allProjects: true. On disk <repo>/.nexusmem/ .gitignore '*' — the workspace ignores itself, so init never edits a file it doesn't own config.json validated on read; a corrupt config fails loudly rather than silently memory.db SQLite in WAL mode ~/.nexusmem/ projects.json which repositories exist, for cross-project recall; a corrupt one reads as empty shell-history.jsonl the hook's log, if you installed it NEXUSMEM_HOME overrides the user-scoped directory. Node ids are content-addressed from sha256(projectId + kind + naturalKey), so running sync twice cannot produce duplicates and ingestion stays correct even if a cursor is lost. Project identity comes from the normalized origin URL when there is one, falling back to the absolute path, so two clones of the same repo share one memory namespace. Deleting .nexusmem/ loses nothing that sync cannot rebuild. Status Ingestion, hybrid retrieval, budgeted packing and the MCP server all work and are covered by 342 tests running on Linux and Windows across Node 22 and 24. Development npm install npm run typecheck npm test npm run build Tests are behavioral rather than snapshot-based, and several are regressions tied to specific observed failures. tests/git-errors.test.ts injects a fake spawn to exercise the Windows process-spawn faults, which cannot be provoked on demand. On how this was built This started as an experiment in whether a local context-memory engine for coding agents was viable, prototyped with Claude Code. The code was written through AI-assisted workflows; the architecture, the design decisions and the specifications were human-directed. That is worth stating plainly because it should change how you read the code, not whether you trust it. Audits, corrections and PRs are genuinely welcome, and the commit history is deliberately detailed about why things are the way they are, including the times an earlier assumption turned out to be wrong. Vectors from two models are not comparable and nodes_vec records no per-row provenance, so sync drops the lot and rebuilds rather than ranking across a mixture. It says so when it happens. A first sync indexes the patches of the most recent 200 commits (later syncs only walk cursor..HEAD); merge commits contribute none, since their patch exists only in a combined format this parser does not read; and binaries, lockfiles and build output are skipped so a dependency bump cannot bury the corpus. All of it is still recorded as a git_commit node. A patch longer than limits.maxBodyChars is truncated, so the tail of a very large change is not indexed. The caps live under sources.diff in config.json.

sentences.en: Diff indexing is bounded, and deliberately lossy.
sentences.zh: 差异索引是有限的，并且故意有损。

sentences.en: A first sync indexes the patches of the most recent 200 commits (later syncs only walk cursor..HEAD); merge commits contribute none, since their patch exists only in a combined format this parser does not read; and binaries, lockfiles and build output are skipped so a dependency bump cannot bury the corpus.

sentences.zh: 所有这些仍然记录为 git_commit 节点。

Each repository's hits are fused by rank, so a project whose best match is mediocre still contributes a rank-1 item, and rank 1 is worth the same in every list. Signal, recency and the budget are what hold that in check; there is no per-project quality weight.

sentences.en: Each repository's hits are fused by rank, so a project whose best match is mediocre still contributes a rank-1 item, and rank 1 is worth the same in every list.

sentences.en: Signal, recency and the budget are what hold that in check; there is no per-project quality weight.

blocks.html_en: • The project registry is an index, not a source of truth. It can point at a database that has moved or been deleted; those are reported and skipped, never silently pruned, because an unmounted drive is not a deleted project.

The cap of 2 is a judgement call, not a measured optimum, same as the ranking priors' budget above.

sentences.en: conversation_turn and doc_section both split one reply or file into several nodes; at most 2 of them may appear together in a packed result.

sentences.en: Found live: a query for "token" returned 9 of its top 12 hits as different pieces of one heavily-sectioned reply, crowding out the node that actually answered it.

blocks.html_en: • The size of the prior budget is a judgement call, not a measured optimum. Priors are now bounded jointly rather than one at a time, which closed a real 4× hole (see the ranking section), but the 2× budget itself has never been tuned against a labelled relevance set — there isn't one. It is a defensible constant, not a result. What is measured is the direction: on four real queries against this repo's own memory, switching to the joint cap moved the section that answered the question up in three of them (the rationale section for "why BM25 before vector search" went from rank 4 to rank 1) and displaced no query's correct top hit.

sentences.en: The size of the prior budget is a judgement call, not a measured optimum.

sentences.en: Priors are now bounded jointly rather than one at a time, which closed a real 4× hole (see the ranking section), but the 2× budget itself has never been tuned against a labelled relevance set — there isn't one.

sentences.en: It is a defensible constant, not a result.

content_html_zh:
我的连接

您的编码代理可以读取 git log。 它无法读取您上周二尝试过但不起作用的四件事。

NexusMem 将您的机器上实际发生的情况（shell 命令及其退出代码、git 历史记录到每个更改文件的补丁、项目文档、可选的助理成绩单）记录到本地 SQLite 数据库中，并根据需要返回排名的、令牌预算的部分。 一切都保留在磁盘上。 没有帐户，没有云，没有遥测。

shell的历史是值得关心的部分。 Git 告诉代理发送了什么。 Shell 历史记录告诉它尝试了什么、按什么顺序以及哪些命令以非零值退出。 该信息不存在于其他地方，并且当您的终端回滚时它就会消失。

Try it

从任何 git 存储库内部：

npx nexusmem init
npx nexusmem sync

然后问它一些事情。 此存储库的实际输出，前 5 个命中中的前 2 个：

$ nexusmem query "windows spawn failure"

Relevant history for: windows spawn failure

- 2026-08-09 fix: distinguish a failed git spawn from "not a git repository"
  readRepoInfo collapsed three unrelated failures into one error: git running and reporting
  the path is not a work tree, git not being installed, and the process failing to spawn at
  all. Dogfooding hit the third case in two separate sessions...
- 2026-08-09 README.md — Before a tagged release
  - [ ] Retry on transient process-spawn failures on Windows

提交和文档部分，在您提供的任何代币预算内相互排名。 模型在退出时没有总结任何内容；排名者刚刚决定不发送什么。 （一个可选来源，会话摘要，确实运行本地模型 - 但在摄取时，永远不会在退出时。 您查询的始终是存储的文本。）

为了了解实际积累的情况，以下是两天后此存储库上的 nexusmem 状态：

527 node(s)  2026-08-08 .. 2026-08-09
       321  shell_command
       130  conversation_turn
        60  doc_section
        16  git_commit

十六次提交。 三百二十一个 shell 命令。 任何具有终端的代理都可以检索这些提交。 其余的则不然。

该 conversation_turn 行仅出现，因为该语料库已与 --conversation 同步。 助理成绩单是默认关闭的一个来源，并且在您选择加入之前一直保持关闭状态，因为它们是最有可能放置粘贴凭证的地方。 默认安装索引 git 提交、它们的差异、shell 和文档。

要求：Node 22 或更高版本，以及 git。 Node 20 将无法工作，因为 better-sqlite3 没有为其提供预构建的二进制文件，并且 Node 20 已于 2026 年 4 月终止生命周期。 Ollama 是可选的，仅影响语义搜索（见下文）。

可选：精确捕获外壳

抓取的历史文件（PSReadLine、.bash_history、.zsh_history）为您提供命令文本，仅此而已。 该钩子为您提供工作目录、退出代码和真实时间戳：

nexusmem hook install

它包装您现有的 PowerShell 提示符而不是替换它，是幂等的，并且 nexusmem hook remove 可以干净地撤消它。

退出代码使得这个值得安装。 失败的命令比成功的命令发出的信号更强，如果没有钩子，就无法区分它们。

检索的工作原理

每个源都标准化为相同的 MemoryNode 形状，因此提交、shell 命令和文档部分平等竞争。 检索在 FTS5 上运行 BM25，如果嵌入模型可达，则在 sqlite-vec 上进行向量搜索，然后使用倒数排名融合将两者融合。

RRF 仅融合排名位置，从不融合原始分数。 这就是它在这里安全的全部原因：BM25 成本和向量距离存在于不相关的、无界的尺度上，并且位置是它们唯一达成一致的事情。 它们之间没有手动调整的归一化常数。

排名乘以三个因素：

score = relevance × signal^0.215 × recency^0.288

相关性来自查询。 信号（修复：提交胜过杂务：；退出非零的命令胜过成功的命令）和新近度是在任何查询存在之前保持的先验。 每个因子都被归入 [floor, 1] 而不是 [0, 1]，因此一个弱维度无法将强匹配归零。

这些指数是导出的，而不是调整的。 先验不断推翻查询：在一个真实查询中，修复：提交从更匹配的文档部分中获得排名 1，信号边缘为 44%，相关性不足为 15%。 因此，先验得到一个共享预算——在整个范围内，它们最多可以推翻 2× 相关性差距——在它们之间平均分配，并且每个先验都被提升到使自己的跨度恰好值得其份额的幂（跨度^指数 = √2）。 先验者仍然像以前一样对同样相关的命中进行排序，因为变换是单调的。 他们只是不能再投票推翻这个问题了。

预算是共享的，而不是按先验的，其原因是通过测试而不是通过阅读算术发现的：分数乘以先验，因此将每个先验的上限分别限制为 2×，从而使这对可以自由地推翻 4×。 这描述了在一个活跃的工作日中所做的每一次承诺——同时具有新鲜感和高信号——因此失败恰恰发生在最值得记住的日子里。 有关 PowerShell 挂钩的查询返回了两个不相关的当天修复：排名为 3 和 4 的提交，而回答该问题的部分位于排名 6。 现在添加第三个之前会重新分配相同的预算，而不是扩大它。

如果没有 Ollama，将跳过矢量搜索，您只能得到 BM25。 该路径得到完全支持，而不是降级错误状态；同步和查询都成功，但做得更少。

会话摘要（可选，本地模型）

通过sources.session.enabled，每个完成的会话都成为原始交换旁边的一个精炼节点——决定了什么以及为什么，而不是四十个单独的回合。 它运行本地 Ollama 聊天模型（默认为 qwen2.5:3b）；不会自动下载任何内容，也不会离开机器。

nexusmem scan-session --dry-run

在编辑和预算调整之后，打印会话将产生的确切提示，而无需调用模型。

三件事限制了成本。 仅当会话安静了结算分钟数（默认 30）后才会对其进行汇总，因此正在进行的会话不会在每次同步时重新汇总。 提示经过哈希处理，未更改的哈希会完全跳过模型 - 在此存储库中，14 个汇总会话的稳态同步需要 0.25 秒，并且不会进行模型调用。 maxSessions（默认 10）限制每次运行到达模型的数量；其余的报告已排队并在下一次同步时拾取。

使用 qwen2.5:3b 在 14 次真实会话中测得的实际情况如何。 摘要本身就很好：带有原因的决策，按照提示要求的形式。 标题不太可靠——模型大约有三分之一的时间返回可用的标题，否则会生成对话式序言、流弹或裸露的“会议摘要”。 这些都被拒绝了，标题又回到了会议开始时问题的第一行，即使它并不优雅，它也总是很具体。 长时间会议和非英语成绩单的合规性最差。 如果标题对您很重要，则较大的模型 (qwen2.5:7b) 是杠杆；设置来源.会话.模型。

从代理处使用

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "nexusmem": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "nexusmem", "mcp"]
    }
  }
}

stdio 上的三个工具：search_memory 返回打包的上下​​文块，sync_project 摄取，get_status 报告当前记住的内容。 每个都采用显式的projectRoot，因为MCP工具调用不携带shell工作目录。 如果尚未设置存储库，sync_project 会为您运行 init。

你要付出什么代价

两个数字在这样的工具中会被混淆，因此它们在这里被分开。

打包器效率是排序器从其自己的候选集中修剪的量。 在此存储库的语料库中，它的运行率为 81-84%。 它对于调整排名很有用，但作为有关您的账单的声明毫无用处，因为基线是假设的：如果没有 NexusMem，这些候选人一开始就不会进入您的上下文窗口。

端到端保存将 NexusMem 实际发送的打包上下文与完整读取的相同文件进行比较，其自己的排名被识别为与查询相关。 使用scripts/benchmark.ts（npm run bench）进行测量，任何克隆此存储库并将其指向同步语料库的人都可以从头开始重新运行：

语料库 提交 查询集 与完整文件内容 与这些文件上的 git log -p 比较
这个仓库 62 16 个真实的提示，逐字来自该项目自身的历史 95%（中位数 94%） 98%（中位数 97%）
vitejs/vite 9,567 16、机械采样——见下文 99%（中位数 98%） ~100%（中位数 ~100%） — 请参阅警告

两者都明确了最初的 >70% 目标（“削减 API 令牌支出与发送完整上下文”），并且 vite 运行是目标始终描述为适用的规模的第一个测量。

在引用任何一个数字之前，请阅读方法论，因为它的范围比看起来要窄：

  • 每个查询的评分依据的文件集来自 NexusMem 自己的排名——无论哪个文件都记录了该查询的打包节点，而不是外部法官对正确答案的想法。 一旦检索已经选择了候选集，这将隔离打包步骤（排名→预算→摘录）保存的内容；它不会独立验证候选集是否是正确的选择。
  • vite 查询集不是手工挑选的：跨完整提交历史记录的均匀样本，将解释良好的修复/功能/性能/重构提交转换为来自提交自己的常规提交文本的“为什么 vite <description>”，加上带有基本原理的文档部分标题。 相反，这个存储库自己的查询集逐字重用来自conversation_turn节点的真实历史提示——其中一些是广泛的任务指令而不是狭隘的问题，这将更广泛的文件集纳入范围，也是其数量虽然仍然很高但低于vite的部分原因。 这两种推导都是机械的，并在 script/benchmark.ts 中公开，也不是针对每个查询精心挑选的。
  • git log -p 在一个被数千次提交触及的文件上是巨大的——一个 vite 查询的基线达到了 750 万个标记，因为其解析集中的文件具有如此多的历史记录。 这本身就是一个发现，而不是噪音：在这种规模下，“只读取文件的历史记录”根本不再是一个可行的替代方案，这也是该专栏四舍五入到 ~100% 的一个重要原因。
  • 这取代了之前约 40% 的数字，该数字是根据针对此存储库的两次精心挑选的查询手工统计的，从未进行过检测，并且使用了未声明的基线。 这并不是错误的，而是未明确说明的——这个数字用规定的方法和重现它的脚本取代了它，而不是声称产品变得更好了。

有一件事不是百分比：shell 命令和会话轮次没有廉价的 grep 等效项。 如果没有任何东西记录它们，它们就会消失，而不仅仅是寻找起来更加昂贵。

大约 530 个节点的语料库上的延迟，热，p50 超过 10 次运行：

手术
BM25 检索 (FTS5) ~1.1 ms
向量 KNN (sqlite-vec) ~3.2 ms
保险丝、等级、包装 ~0.6 ms
查询嵌入（本地 Ollama） ~55–77 ms
端到端混合 ~56 ms

所有 SQLite 工作总共大约 5 毫秒。 嵌入调用是这条路径上唯一值得优化的东西，而且它是其他人的过程。

哪里破裂了

  • 没有钩子的 shell 历史记录是无作用域的。 抓取的历史记录没有目录上下文，因此它归因于您从中运行同步的任何存储库。 受限于尾窗，并且是近似值而不是保证。
  • 日语和中文取决于矢量通行证。 FTS5 的 unicode61 分词器会根据空格进行分割，因此没有空格边界的语言无法进行有用的 BM25 召回。
  • 重新调整股线节点的基准。 重写的历史记录留下了无法访问的提交的节点。 他们描述了真实的事件，因此他们没有错，但有针对性的修剪还不存在。 sync --rebuild 强制进行干净的重新扫描。
  • 多行 PowerShell 输入被读取为单独的命令。 在提示符下跨多行键入的函数不会被重建。
  • 如果在同步之间从前面修剪历史文件，则抓取后备 ID 会发生漂移。 安装钩子可以解决这个问题。
  • 会话摘要标题取决于遵循说明的模型，而 3B 模型通常则不然。 后备使它们保持特定而不是通用，但请参阅上面的部分以了解预期内容。
  • 更改嵌入模型会重新嵌入所有内容。 来自两个模型的向量不具有可比性，并且nodes_vec 不记录每行的出处，因此同步会丢弃批次并重建，而不是在混合物中排名。 当事情发生时它会这么说。 节点未受影响，BM25 始终保持工作状态。
  • 差异索引是有限的，并且故意有损。 第一次同步索引最近 200 个提交的补丁（稍后仅同步游标..HEAD）；合并提交没有贡献，因为它们的补丁仅以该解析器无法读取的组合格式存在；并且二进制文件、锁定文件和构建输出都会被跳过，因此依赖项碰撞不会掩盖语料库。 所有这些仍然记录为 git_commit 节点。 长度超过 limit.maxBodyChars 的补丁将被截断，因此非常大的更改的尾部不会被索引。 这些上限位于 config.json 中的sources.diff 下。
  • 跨项目回忆有利于广度。 每个存储库的点击量都按排名融合，因此最佳匹配平庸的项目仍然会贡献排名 1 的项目，并且排名 1 在每个列表中的价值相同。 添加一个与您的问题没什么可说的存储库仍然会将其一些结果推入预算。 信号、新近度和预算是控制因素；没有每个项目的质量权重。
  • 项目注册表是一个索引，而不是事实来源。 它可以指向已移动或已删除的数据库；这些被报告并跳过，永远不会默默地修剪，因为卸载的驱动器不是已删除的项目。
  • 对话分块未被评估。 在标题边界处拆分长回复确实有帮助，但从未经过系统测试。
  • 一个结果中分块节点的同级计数是有上限的，而不是调整。 conversation_turn 和 doc_section 都将一个回复或文件拆分为多个节点；其中最多 2 个可能一起出现在打包结果中。 实时发现：对“token”的查询返回了前 12 个命中中的 9 个，作为一个厚重分段回复的不同部分，从而挤出了实际回答它的节点。 2 的上限是一个判断，而不是衡量的最佳值，与上面排名先验的预算相同。
  • 先前预算的大小是一个判断，而不是衡量的最佳值。 先验现在是共同限制的，而不是一次一个，这弥补了一个真正的 4× 漏洞（参见排名部分），但 2× 预算本身从未针对标记的相关性集进行调整 - 没有一个。 它是一个可辩护的常数，而不是一个结果。 衡量的是方向：在针对此存储库自己的内存的四个真实查询中，切换到联合上限将其中三个中回答问题的部分移至上位（“为什么向量搜索之前的 BM25”的基本原理部分从排名 4 上升到排名 1），并且没有取代任何查询的正确热门命中。

初始化、同步、查询<文本>、状态、项目、mcp 和挂钩安装|删除|状态。

跨项目回忆

query --all-projects 搜索您运行 NexusMem 的每个存储库，而不仅仅是当前存储库，并使用其来自的存储库标记每个结果：

$ nexusmem query --all-projects "why was the retry budget raised"
scope   2 project(s): NexusMem, uploader

- 2026-08-12 [uploader] fix: raise the retry budget after the S3 upload timeouts
- 2026-08-12 [uploader] retry.ts @ 8d0f98b — fix: raise the retry budget after the S3 upload timeouts
  @@ -1 +1 @@
  -export const RETRY_BUDGET = 3;
  +export const RETRY_BUDGET = 5;
- 2026-08-09 [NexusMem] fix(git): retry a transient failure to spawn git

数据库保留在每个存储库中 - 没有共享的全局存储，并且删除一个存储库的 .nexusmem/ 仍然会准确删除该存储库的内存。 使其他内容可找到的是 ~/.nexusmem/projects.json 中的普通索引，由 init 编写并由每次同步刷新。 nexusmem 项目显示其中的内容，并且 --prune 会忘记数据库已消失的条目。

跨存储库排名使用每个项目的倒数排名融合，而不是原始 BM25，因为 BM25 成本是根据其自己的语料库计算的，并且在 50 节点和 50,000 节点数据库中意味着不同的事情。 该交易在其中断位置中进行了说明。

MCP search_memory 工具采用与 allProjects: true 相同的开关。

在磁盘上

<repo>/.nexusmem/
  .gitignore     '*' — the workspace ignores itself, so init never edits a file it doesn't own
  config.json    validated on read; a corrupt config fails loudly rather than silently
  memory.db      SQLite in WAL mode

~/.nexusmem/
  projects.json      which repositories exist, for cross-project recall; a corrupt one reads as empty
  shell-history.jsonl  the hook's log, if you installed it

NEXUSMEM_HOME 覆盖用户范围的目录。

节点 ID 是根据 sha256(projectId + kind + naturalKey) 进行内容寻址的，因此运行两次同步不会产生重复，并且即使光标丢失，摄取也能保持正确。 项目标识来自规范化的原始 URL（当有一个项目时），回落到绝对路径，因此同一存储库的两个克隆共享一个内存命名空间。

删除 .nexusmem/ 不会丢失同步无法重建的任何内容。

关于这是如何构建的

这是一个实验，旨在研究用于编码代理的本地上下文记忆引擎是否可行，并以 Claude Code 为原型。 代码是通过人工智能辅助工作流程编写的；架构、设计决策和规范都是以人为主导的。

这值得明确说明，因为它应该改变您阅读代码的方式，而不是您是否信任它。 审计、更正和 PR 是真正受欢迎的，并且提交历史记录是故意详细说明为什么事情是这样的，包括早期假设被证明是错误的时间。
